page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-dense virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting standard x86_64 instructions such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512 extensions. The instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached volumes, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark metrics indicate moderate overall throughput with distinct trade-offs due to shared CPU provisioning. Geekbench yields 1,807.0 for single-core and 10,963.0 for multi-core performance, highlighted by top-tier text processing at 2,886.0 points. Conversely, raw CPU stress tests show constrained performance, with stress-ng recording 764.28 single-core and 6,050.82 multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth reaches 78.48 GB/sec for 256 MB sequential reads and 40.34 GB/sec for writes, although the PassMark memory suite registers in the lower quartile at 1,357.53. In-memory operations demonstrate solid utility, achieving 11.14 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.49 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not demand continuous, high-frequency compute cycles. The lack of bundled local storage and accelerator hardware makes it unsuited for heavy disk I/O or GPU computation. Optimal workloads include distributed in-memory caching tiers, large Redis deployments, text processing pipelines, intermediate data transformation, and memory-intensive staging environments.

It delivers 8 shared vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a substantial 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on external network block storage for persistence. In synthetic evaluations, it achieves balanced baseline results, with 10,963.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 11.14 million Redis SET operations per second, though stress-ng scores reflect the limitations of shared CPU allocation. Its high memory footprint delivers qualitative economic value for memory-dominant tasks that avoid sustained CPU saturation. The CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is well aligned for large in-memory caches, database read replicas, text parsing workflows, and data processing stages requiring expansive working memory.
